countries.name: Philippines
countries.summary: The Philippines is a leading English-medium study destination in Southeast Asia, known internationally for nursing and allied-health education. Its CHED-regulated universities teach in English, follow a four-year bachelor's structure, and route Nursing graduates toward the Philippine Nurse Licensure Examination administered by the Professional Regulation Commission.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: English-medium instruction removes the language barrier common to non-English destinations, while CHED-recognized four-year Bachelor of Science in Nursing programmes combine campus skills-lab training with hospital-based Related Learning Experience at teaching and partner hospitals. Tuition and living costs are generally lower than English-speaking Western destinations, and graduates sit the Philippine Nurse Licensure Examination as a recognized regional credential.
countries.climate: Tropical climate with a distinct wet season (roughly June to November) and dry season (December to May); typhoons are most frequent during the wet season, most often affecting Luzon.

universities.name: Angeles University Foundation
universities.summary: Angeles University Foundation is a private Catholic university in Angeles City, Pampanga, founded in 1962. Its Bachelor of Science in Nursing holds PAASCU Level IV accreditation, CHED Center of Development status and CHED Autonomous Status, with clinical training anchored by AUF's own 125-bed teaching hospital and public partner hospitals across Central Luzon.
universities.campusLifestyle: AUF's MacArthur Highway campus sits about 10 minutes from the Clark Freeport Zone, roughly 81 km north of Metro Manila. The College of Nursing teaches from the San Lorenzo and San Agustin Halls, backed by a four-storey library holding over 103,000 volumes, an Information Technology Training Center, a CI-AUF Language Laboratory and the AUF Sports and Cultural Center.
universities.cityProfile: Angeles City, Pampanga anchors Central Luzon's Clark corridor, about 10 minutes from the Clark Freeport Zone, home to Clark International Airport. The zone's proximity shortens international travel connections and shapes daily campus life. AUF's own 125-bed AUF Medical Center, inaugurated in 1990 as the first private tertiary teaching hospital in Central Luzon, anchors the campus precinct alongside public hospitals used for wider clinical rotations.
universities.practicalExposure: Related Learning Experience (RLE) runs through AUF's own Nursing Arts Laboratories: four air-conditioned skills labs with an attached hospital-simulation room replicating an operating room, delivery room, nursery and emergency room, plus dedicated Nutrition Laboratories and Anatomy and Physiology Rooms. Hospital-based RLE draws on the 125-bed AUF Medical Center on campus alongside named public affiliate sites: Jose B. Lingad Memorial Regional Hospital, Ospital Ning Angeles, Mabalacat District Hospital, Balitucan District Hospital, Diosdado P. Macapagal District Hospital, Ricardo P. Rodriguez Memorial District Hospital, the National Center for Mental Health, Philippine Orthopedic Hospital and San Lazaro Hospital, giving students rotations across private, district and specialty-hospital settings rather than one placement site.
universities.hostelOverview: AUF operates three secured, Wi-Fi-ready dormitory sites near the main campus with combined capacity for up to 355 residents; specific room rates are not published online and should be confirmed directly with the Admissions Office. No verified nearby private boarding-house rate range is available from official sources at this time.
universities.dietarySupport: AUF's campus sits along MacArthur Highway near the Clark Freeport Zone, giving students access to the wider Angeles City food and retail corridor; the university has not published a specific on-campus meal plan or dining-cost figure. Daily living costs should be planned separately from tuition until AUF's Admissions Office issues a current cost breakdown.
universities.safetyOverview: AUF's Office of University Health Services provides on-campus medical and dental services, and the Office of Student Affairs runs orientation, welcome programming and grievance handling. No campus-specific safety statistics are published; the campus sits in an urban corridor near the Clark Freeport Zone rather than an isolated setting.
universities.studentSupport: The Guidance and Counseling Center (Mon-Fri 8am-7pm, Sat 8am-5pm) supports students alongside the Office of Student Affairs. International applicants route through the Office of the University Registrar, which processes Special Study Permit and 9(f) student-visa paperwork, and AUF's Office of International Affairs, which handles foreign admissions.

faq.question: Is Angeles University Foundation's BS Nursing program accredited?
faq.answer: Yes. It holds PAASCU Level IV accreditation, PAASCU's highest level, continuously held since January 1995 and valid through May 2031. The program is also a CHED-designated Center of Development in Nursing Education.

faq.question: How long is the BSN program?
faq.answer: Four years, following the Philippines' national CHED curriculum policy for the Bachelor of Science in Nursing degree.

faq.question: Do international applicants need IELTS or TOEFL?
faq.answer: AUF's official foreign-admissions materials list an English Proficiency Test as required only 'where necessary,' not as a blanket rule for every nationality. Confirm current policy with AUF's Office of International Affairs before assuming an exemption.

faq.question: When can international students start the BSN program?
faq.answer: AUF's foreign-admissions primer lists two bachelor's-degree intakes: June (First Semester) and November (Second Semester). Reconfirm exact current dates with AUF's Registrar, since this primer is only accessible through an archived copy at the time of research.

faq.question: What visa do foreign BSN students need?
faq.answer: Typically a Philippine 9(f) student visa, processed through AUF's Office of the University Registrar, which also handles Special Study Permit processing for international students.

faq.question: Where do AUF nursing students complete their clinical training?
faq.answer: Primarily at the 125-bed AUF Medical Center on campus, plus named affiliated public hospitals including Jose B. Lingad Memorial Regional Hospital, Ospital Ning Angeles, and several district and specialty hospitals across Central Luzon.

faq.question: Does AUF publish BS Nursing tuition fees online?
faq.answer: No. AUF does not publish a public BSN tuition or fee schedule on its website; a current cost plan is available directly from AUF's Admissions and Accounting Office.

faq.question: Does AUF have on-campus housing?
faq.answer: Yes — three dormitory sites near the main campus, accommodating up to 355 residents combined, though specific rates are not published online and should be confirmed with the Admissions Office.

faq.question: What is AUF's nurse licensure exam track record?
faq.answer: AUF's College of Nursing was named Top Performing School nationwide in the November 2023 Nursing Licensure Examination by the Professional Regulation Commission's Board of Nursing, with independent reporting also showing AUF among schools posting 100% passing rates in several recent exam cycles.

faq.question: What academic background do BS Nursing applicants need?
faq.answer: AUF's AY2026-2027 criteria require a STEM Senior High School strand for Philippine-curriculum applicants. Foreign applicants are evaluated case-by-case on academic-record equivalency by the College of Nursing Dean rather than against a fixed published rule for BSN specifically.

evidence.claimText: Angeles University Foundation was established May 25, 1962 and granted University status April 16, 1971; it is a private, non-stock, non-profit Catholic university, the first Catholic university in Central Luzon, on MacArthur Highway, Angeles City, Pampanga.

CHED granted AUF Autonomous Status in 2003. AUF's own University Profile also states its Nursing programme is a CHED-designated Center of Development and holds FAAP institutional accreditation and ISO 9001:2015 certification (TUV-SUD).
BS Nursing holds PAASCU Level IV accreditation (PAASCU's highest level), initial accreditation January 1995, current validity through May 2031.

evidence.sourceLabel: AUF official Admission page and Foreign Student Admissions primer
